```plato
//==
// # Intrinsics — the host contract
//
// An **intrinsic** is a function the language declares but does not define: a
// signature terminated by `;` with no `=>` body, inside a `library` block. The
// host runtime supplies the implementation. This file is the complete contract a
// backend must satisfy — for C# that is the handwritten `Plato.Intrinsics`;
// for a new backend (C++, GLSL, Rust) it is the porting checklist.
//
// **Rule: a bodiless intrinsic may mention only `primitive` types** (Number,
// Integer, Boolean, Character, String, Array, Buffer, List, Function0-9,
// Type — see `primitives.plato`).
//
// **Admission rule (plato-378): an intrinsic must not be expressible in Plato
// from the other intrinsics.** If a portable reference body exists, the function
// belongs in a `*.library.plato` file and the backend recovers native speed
// through its override table (plato-368), not by growing this list. Everything
// on Angle, Number2/3/4/8, Vector2D/3D, Matrix3x2/4x4 and Quaternion left under
// that rule; the array reshaping family and the derivable scalar surface
// followed it. `IntrinsicsSurfaceTests` pins the count so the list cannot drift
// back up.
//
// Target backends, in priority order: C#, C++, CUDA, TypeScript, then GLSL, Rust,
// Python (see README.md "Target backends"). An intrinsic belongs here only if every
// priority-1..4 target can supply it natively or with a trivial shim; anything
// C#-specific stays out (see the notes at the bottom of this file).
//
// Bodiless declarations inside a `interface` are NOT intrinsics — those are
// obligations on whoever implements the interface, and the stdlib satisfies them in
// Plato. Only `library` blocks declare host intrinsics.
//
// This is the ONLY file in the library with bodiless declarations, and it stays
// that way.

library Intrinsics
{
    //==
    // Number — the irreducible scalar kernel.
    //
    // Everything derivable from these has a reference body in
    // `primitives.library.plato`: Abs, Sign, Square, Reciprocal, Min,
    // Max, Ceiling, Truncate, Log/Log2/Log10, the Tan/Cosh/Sinh/Tanh
    // family, the whole inverse-trig family (over Atan2Radians and NaturalLog),
    // Zero/One/Tau/E, IsFinite, and the five relational operators the IOrderable
    // generics already cover.

    Add(a: Number, b: Number): Number;
```
